meta.description: Allow administrators to look up and permanently delete an existing user account from the CardDemo system's user security file.
meta.process_description: The program presents an administrator with a user deletion screen where they can enter a User ID to look up. Upon entering a User ID and pressing Enter, the system retrieves and displays the user's details (first name, last name, user type) from the security file, prompting the administrator to confirm deletion. The administrator must then explicitly press PF5 to confirm and execute the permanent deletion of the user account. Upon successful deletion, the screen is cleared and a confirmation message is displayed; the administrator can cancel at any time by pressing PF3 or PF12 to return to the previous screen.

files.USRSEC: User security file storing all system user accounts including credentials, names, and user type (admin/regular)

business_rules: A User ID must be provided before any lookup or deletion can be performed; an empty User ID is rejected with an error message.
The administrator must perform a two-step confirmation: first look up the user (Enter key) to verify the correct account is displayed, then explicitly press PF5 to execute the permanent deletion.
If the specified User ID does not exist in the security file, the deletion is rejected with a 'User ID NOT found' error message.
Deletion is permanent and irreversible; once confirmed via PF5, the user record is removed from the USRSEC file with no soft-delete or archival mechanism.
The program can only be accessed from within an authenticated session; if no communication area is present (EIBCALEN = 0), the user is redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C).
Upon successful deletion, all screen fields are cleared, preventing accidental re-submission or confusion about the current state.
PF3 and PF12 both return the administrator to the previous screen (typically the admin menu COADM01C), allowing cancellation without deletion.
PF4 clears the current screen input, allowing the administrator to start a new lookup without navigating away.
The program uses a CICS UPDATE lock when reading the user record prior to deletion, ensuring no concurrent modifications can occur between the lookup and the delete operation.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group holding all operational variables used by the Delete User program (COUSR03C) during an administrator's session to look up and permanently remove a user account.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program ('COUSR03C'), used when transferring control between CICS programs or logging errors, so the system always knows which program is currently executing the user deletion function.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier ('CU03') assigned to the Delete User function. This is the 4-character code an administrator would use to invoke the delete user screen directly, and it is displayed on the screen header so the administrator knows which transaction they are in.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The feedback message displayed at the bottom of the Delete User screen to communicate the outcome of an action to the administrator — for example, confirming a successful deletion, reporting that the User ID was not found, or prompting the administrator to enter a User ID before proceeding.

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The name of the User Security file ('USRSEC') that stores all system user accounts, including credentials, names, and user types. This value is used when issuing CICS file control commands to look up or permanently delete a user record from the system.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator flag that tracks whether a validation or system error has occurred during the current delete user operation. When set to 'Y', it signals that the screen should be redisplayed with an error message rather than proceeding with the deletion.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when an error has been detected during the delete user process — such as a missing User ID, a User ID not found in the security file, or a file system error — causing the program to halt the deletion and display an appropriate error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when no errors have been detected, indicating the delete user process is proceeding normally and the program can continue to the next step, such as displaying the retrieved user details or executing the permanent deletion.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each file operation (such as reading or deleting a user record from USRSEC). The program inspects this code to determine whether the operation succeeded, the record was not found, or an unexpected system error occurred, driving the appropriate error handling and user feedback.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code that accompanies the response code, providing additional detail about why a file operation failed. Together with WS-RESP-CD, it helps diagnose specific error conditions when reading or deleting a user account from the security file.

variables.name: WS-USR-MODIFIED
variables.description: A session-level flag that records whether a user account deletion has been successfully carried out during the current administrator session. When set to 'Y', it signals that a record was permanently removed from the USRSEC file, which can be used to trigger confirmation messaging or influence screen behavior after the deletion.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-YES
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when a user account has been successfully and permanently deleted from the security file during the current session, allowing the program to display a deletion confirmation message and clear the screen fields.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-NO
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when no user account deletion has yet been performed in the current session, indicating the administrator is still in the lookup or confirmation phase and no permanent changes have been made to the security file.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-INFO
variables.description: A group of fields specific to the Delete User function (CU03) that carry contextual information about the current user list browsing state and the selected user account targeted for deletion, typically passed between the user list screen (COUSR00C) and this delete program.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-USRID-FIRST
variables.description: The User ID of the first user account displayed on the current page of the user list screen (COUSR00C). This is used to maintain the administrator's position in the user list so they can return to the correct page after completing or cancelling a deletion.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-USRID-LAST
variables.description: The User ID of the last user account displayed on the current page of the user list screen (COUSR00C). Together with CDEMO-CU03-USRID-FIRST, it defines the range of user accounts currently visible, enabling correct pagination when the administrator returns to the list.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The current page number within the user list that the administrator was viewing when they selected a user for deletion. This allows the system to return the administrator to the same page of the user list after the deletion is completed or cancelled.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether additional pages of user accounts exist beyond the current page in the user list. This supports pagination in the calling user list screen (COUSR00C), ensuring the administrator can navigate forward through the full list of system users.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when there are more user accounts available beyond the current page in the user list, enabling the 'next page' navigation option on the user list screen.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the current page is the last page of user accounts in the list, meaning there are no further records to display and the 'next page' navigation option should be suppressed.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-USR-SEL-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the administrator has actively selected a specific user account from the user list screen for deletion. When set, it confirms that the User ID in CDEMO-CU03-USR-SELECTED was deliberately chosen rather than being a default or empty value.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU03-USR-SELECTED
variables.description: The User ID pre-selected and passed in from the calling user list screen (COUSR00C) identifying the specific user account the administrator has chosen to delete. This value pre-populates the User ID field on the Delete User screen, streamlining the deletion workflow.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed between programs when control is transferred. Its presence (EIBCALEN > 0) confirms the administrator is operating within an authenticated CardDemo session; if absent, the user is redirected to the sign-on screen. It carries session context such as the logged-in user's identity and the calling program name.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: A single-byte placeholder representing the communication area data passed from the calling program. It is defined minimally here because the actual communication area structure (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA from COCOM01Y) is overlaid on top of it, allowing the program to access the full session context including the logged-in administrator's identity and navigation state.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration paragraph of the user deletion program. It determines the session context, interprets the administrator's input, and routes processing to the appropriate action — whether that is displaying the deletion screen, looking up a user, confirming deletion, clearing the screen, or returning to the previous menu.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the administrator's initial User ID lookup request by validating that a User ID has been entered, retrieving the matching user account from the security file, and displaying the account details (name and user type) on screen so the administrator can confirm they are deleting the correct person.

paragraphs.name: DELETE-USER-INFO
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the user account deletion process by first validating that a User ID has been provided, then retrieving the user record from the security file and permanently removing it. It acts as the central coordinator for the two-step deletion workflow, enforcing mandatory input before any file operations are attempted.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the navigation logic when an administrator cancels or completes the user deletion process, transferring control back to the appropriate previous screen. It ensures the system always has a valid destination to return to, defaulting to the sign-on screen if no prior navigation context exists.

paragraphs.name: SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the User Deletion screen to the administrator's terminal, displaying any relevant status or error messages alongside the current screen data. It is the final step in preparing the visual interface before the administrator can enter a User ID or confirm a deletion.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-USRDEL-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the administrator's input from the user deletion screen, reading whatever the administrator has typed or the function key they have pressed. It is the entry point for processing any administrator action on the delete user form, whether that is entering a User ID to look up, confirming a deletion, or cancelling.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the header section of the user deletion screen with current date, time, application title, transaction identifier, and program name, ensuring the administrator always sees accurate contextual information at the top of the screen before any user lookup or deletion action is performed.

paragraphs.name: READ-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves a user account from the security file using an exclusive lock, preventing concurrent changes, and displays the account details to the administrator for deletion confirmation. Depending on whether the account is found or not, it either prompts the administrator to confirm deletion via PF5, or displays an appropriate error message.

paragraphs.name: DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph executes the permanent, irreversible deletion of a user account from the security file and handles all possible outcomes: confirming success to the administrator, reporting that the user was not found, or surfacing an unexpected system error.

paragraphs.name: CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Resets the user deletion screen to a blank state after a deletion is completed or when a fresh lookup is needed, preventing any residual user data from remaining visible and avoiding accidental re-submission. This ensures the administrator sees a clean, empty form ready for the next action.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: Resets the user deletion screen to a completely blank state, clearing all previously displayed user details and any status messages. This ensures the administrator starts with a clean slate, preventing confusion or accidental re-use of data from a prior lookup or deletion.
